IsMarkovTrace restricts strip, stable and cyclic to Supp-n words and adds the Hecke quadratic, braid and far-commutation relations. It proves tr(sigma_n^2) = hz + 1, the product law for an ascending run, non-vacuity via the trivial character, and the counter-model showing strip + cyclic + embed are not enough. It leaves the general law as the open proposition DisjointProductLaw (bean qou-tmmt). Termination is the constant 'some default' tracer and is labelled as shape only. But lean.ref still resolves to the library theorem QOU.BraidKnot.markovTraceRecursiveReducer. It returns ctx.claim_reducer_correct, a class field asserting termination, correctness and disjoint-product preservation, so it is self-assuming, as before. The statement still claims the general disjoint-product property, and its own 'Disjoint-product property' section still gives the z-factor induction argument. The new section below it says that argument is wrong for repeated generators and the general law is not formalised, so the md contradicts itself. A sibling docstring (about line 371) still says 'markovTrace_disjointProduct below now does ... the product law is proved'; no such declaration exists.
